_comment: Single transactions and cross-shard deposits driven through
declares whether it pins a successful execution or a rejection.

cases.name: in_shard_transfer
cases.comment: plain in-shard QKC transfer: nonce increments before gas is bought, fee lands in the coinbase and in block_fee_tokens

cases.name: in_shard_transfer_nonce_too_high
cases.comment: apply_transaction re-validates, so a future nonce is rejected and nothing is written

cases.name: in_shard_transfer_insufficient_balance
cases.comment: the balance check covers value plus the whole gas budget

cases.name: xshard_deposit_to_empty_account
cases.comment: post-EVM deposit: the value is credited to the sender on this shard first, then moved by an EVM message (messages.py:368-377)

cases.name: native_token_transfer_with_default_gas
cases.comment: a foreign transfer token with the chain's own token for gas: no conversion, the fee stays in QKC and only the transfer moves QETH

cases.name: native_token_transfer_sender_holds_none
cases.comment: validate_transaction (4): a token the sender holds none of is refused outright, where the chain's own token is spendable from empty

result.error: <Transaction(0cf8)>: non-default token QETH has zero balance

cases.name: native_token_as_gas_converted
cases.comment: gas paid in QETH: the manager is asked for a price, sells the genesis token that funds the frame and keeps the QETH, and the unused gas comes back at the rate it named — 80%, with the other 20% burned to the zero address (messages.py:438-460, 268)

cases.name: native_token_as_gas_priced_at_zero
cases.comment: the manager answering zero is a refusal, not free gas (messages.py:243)

result.error: <Transaction(1857)>: non-default gas token QETH not ready for being used to pay gas

cases.name: native_token_as_gas_reserve_too_small
cases.comment: the manager has a price but not enough genesis token to settle the whole allowance at it (messages.py:253)

result.error: <Transaction(1857)>: non-default gas token QETH not enough reserve balance for conversion

cases.name: mnt_balance_precompile
cases.comment: the balance precompile reads any token for any address at a flat 400 gas (specials.py:365)

cases.name: mnt_mint_precompile_rejects_foreign_sender
cases.comment: minting is the auction contract's alone: called by anyone else the frame fails and its whole allowance is gone (specials.py:356)

cases.name: transfer_mnt_refusal_keeps_the_rest_of_the_gas
cases.comment: the transfer-token precompile refusing for want of balance costs only the call surcharge and hands the rest back (specials.py:264): the caller can still afford the store that follows, which it could not if the refusal had burned the frame

cases.name: deploy_system_contract_returns_its_address
cases.comment: the deploy precompile answers with the address it deployed to, not with the code it deployed (messages.py:783), and a contract can read that off the return data

cases.name: create_under_a_shard_key
cases.comment: a CREATE in an ordinary frame derives its address from rlp([sender, full_shard_key, nonce]) (messages.py:704). Paired with the case below, which reaches the same code without a key

cases.name: create_under_transfer_mnt_has_no_shard_key
cases.comment: the transfer-token precompile builds its child message without a shard key (specials.py:265), so the same code deploys to Ethereum's rlp([sender, nonce]) address instead — a different account and a different state root

cases.name: contract_creation
cases.comment: a deployment: the address is keccak(rlp([sender, full_shard_key, nonce]))[12:], the top-level nonce does not move for the CREATE itself, and the receipt carries the address and its shard key (messages.py:704)

cases.name: contract_call_returns_value
cases.comment: calling deployed code: the return data reaches the caller and the gas actually burned is what the receipt records

cases.name: contract_revert
cases.comment: a reverting call is a failed transaction, not a rejected one: the state goes back, the gas is gone and the receipt says so

cases.name: contract_out_of_gas
cases.comment: running out of gas costs the whole allowance and leaves the value where it started

cases.name: contract_selfdestruct
cases.comment: the suicide list is applied after the message, not at the opcode (messages.py:351): the balance moves to the beneficiary and del_account strips the account, which the end-of-block sweep then drops

cases.name: contract_logs_and_bloom
cases.comment: one log with one topic: the receipt's bloom and the block's are built from it

cases.name: contract_create2
cases.comment: CREATE2 from inside a frame: unlike a top-level CREATE, a nested one moves the creator's nonce

cases.name: create2_word_gas_underflows
cases.comment: CREATE2's per-word charge is subtracted unchecked and the memory it is charged for needs no growing, so the frame carries a negative gas counter past the point anything would notice it; with CREATE2 last, the frame hands that counter back and apply_transaction trips its own `assert gas_remained >= 0` (messages.py:305). The transaction is not refused for a reason -- pyquarkchain cannot process it at all, so no block containing it exists

cases.name: create2_word_gas_covered
cases.comment: the same code with the word charge paid for, which is what makes the case above readable: same frame, 500 more gas, and the deployment goes through normally

cases.name: create2_word_gas_oog_while_growing
cases.comment: the same shortfall with the memory still to grow: mem_extend checks before it spends, so both sides simply run out of gas and the transaction is processed with a failed receipt. This is the case that keeps the boundary above from swallowing an ordinary out-of-gas and abandoning a block that is fine

cases.name: nested_call
cases.comment: a call inside a call: the inner frame's gas comes out of the outer one's and both are settled once, at the top

cases.name: eip155_transfer
cases.comment: a version 2 (EIP155) transaction, which devnet enables at genesis: the sender is recovered under Ethereum's rules and the shard keys must both be zero (messages.py:139-183)

cases.name: eip155_before_enable_timestamp
cases.comment: mainnet only enables the EIP155 signer in 2021; before that the version is refused whatever else it says

result.error: EIP155 Signer is not enable yet.

cases.name: eip155_non_default_token
cases.comment: the EIP155 signer has no field for a token, so both must be the chain's own

result.error: EIP155 Signer only support QKC as transfer token.

cases.name: eip155_non_zero_shard_key
cases.comment: a non-zero shard key is how a version 2 transaction would become cross-shard, which the signer does not support

result.error: EIP155 Signer do not support cross shard transaction.

cases.name: xshard_source_transfer
cases.comment: the source half of a cross-shard transfer: the value leaves, a deposit carries the whole remaining allowance to the target, and the surcharge is left out of both the fee and gas_used (messages.py:520-560)

cases.name: xshard_source_contract_creation
cases.comment: a cross-shard deployment: the address is derived here, from the sender's nonce as it now stands, and the code is deployed on the target (messages.py:494)

cases.name: xshard_deposit_failed_message_leaves_funds_with_sender
cases.comment: the deposit credits the sender on this shard first and only then moves the value by a message; when that message fails the money stays with the sender here rather than going back (messages.py:368-377)

cases.name: mnt_balance_precompile_pads_short_calldata
cases.comment: the balance precompile reads its arguments with extract32 (vm.py:59), so calldata that stops after the address is not refused: the token id reads as zero and the call succeeds at the same flat 400 gas

cases.name: mnt_mint_precompile_pads_short_calldata
cases.comment: the mint precompile reads its amount with extract32 as well: 80 bytes of calldata leaves the amount word half off the end, and what is minted is that half padded with zeros, not a refusal

cases.name: sstore_legacy_pricing
cases.comment: SSTORE is metered the pre-EIP-1283 way — 20000 for a clean zero to non-zero, 5000 otherwise, and a flat 15000 refund for clearing — including for a slot the same transaction writes twice

cases.name: returndatacopy_within_the_answer
cases.comment: copying exactly as many bytes as the last call returned is in range (vm.py:542)

cases.name: returndatacopy_past_the_answer
cases.comment: one byte past what the last call returned is an exception, and an exception costs the frame everything it had left

cases.name: create_init_code_reverts
cases.comment: init code that reverts leaves no contract and pushes zero, and the creating frame keeps what the init code did not spend (messages.py:793)

cases.name: create_code_store_out_of_gas
cases.comment: paying for the deployed code is all or nothing: too little gas for the 200-per-byte charge reverts the deployment and takes the rest of the gas with it (messages.py:781)

cases.name: create_code_too_large
cases.comment: one byte over the 24576 limit fails the same way, whatever gas is left
